topic: A ref transaction is committed if and only
canonical_claim: A ref transaction is committed if and only if it is reachable from the namespace's exact-read _head.; The immutable node PUT is not the commit point: a writer conditionally creates the node, token-CASes _head to the new tip, and acknowledges only after the exact head shows the proposed tip and local installation is complete.; The selected CAS ref design uses one exact-readable pool catalog, one fixed mutable head per namespace, immutable predecessor-linked transaction nodes, and a head CAS as the transaction commit point; LIST discovers garbage candidates only.

topic: The ref-node sequence is dense and per-incarnation, with
canonical_claim: The ref-node sequence is dense and per-incarnation, with node.sequence = parent.sequence + 1; failed candidate nodes do not create committed-chain gaps.

topic: The namespace head must update monotonically: transaction updates
canonical_claim: The namespace head must update monotonically: transaction updates point to a node whose previous is the old tip, checkpoint updates preserve the tip and advance coverage only, and recovery fences preserve tip/checkpoint while changing writer_epoch.

topic: ref_catalog is a sorted map from logical namespace
canonical_claim: ref_catalog is a sorted map from logical namespace to random 128-bit incarnation and contains active namespaces plus namespaces waiting for terminal removal to fold, without permanent tombstones.

topic: Namespace creation chooses a random incarnation, creates or
canonical_claim: Namespace creation chooses a random incarnation, creates or CAS-replaces _head with an empty head, CAS-adds {namespace, incarnation} to ref_catalog, and waits for an exact catalog read-back before the first owner transaction commits.

topic: Recovery exact-reads ref_catalog, _head, and the checkpoint named
canonical_claim: Recovery exact-reads ref_catalog, _head, and the checkpoint named by _head, follows exact node links while verifying namespace, incarnation, body hash, dense sequence, and acyclicity, then CAS-fences _head with the new writer_epoch before installing state.

topic: encodeFoldSeal writes a meta line containing g/pg between
canonical_claim: `encodeFoldSeal` writes a meta line containing `g`/`pg` between the header and trailer, and `foldSealFixedBytes` is a floor measured at `generation = 0` and `n = 0`, not a constant for every seal.

topic: The raw fixture publishAt is not the production
canonical_claim: The raw fixture `publishAt` is not the production birth writer: it drains through `writeRefLogTxnRaw`, whose test-only `casAdmitEntry` call admits the namespace into the catalog.

topic: writeRefSnapshotRaw does not admit a catalog entry; a
canonical_claim: `writeRefSnapshotRaw` does not admit a catalog entry; a caller needing the namespace to be discoverable must call `casAdmitEntry` first, as `writeRefLogTxnRaw` does.

topic: The runtime size fences drive only the birth-time
canonical_claim: The runtime size fences drive only the birth-time `_ckpt` writer; fixed-capacity non-heap fields populated by the sealer or snapshot publisher are outside those three fences.

topic: completeCreation publishes a namespace _ckpt at creation, before
canonical_claim: `completeCreation` publishes a namespace `_ckpt` at creation, before any first snapshot publication commits.

topic: ref_publish and ref_drop audit events currently carry no
canonical_claim: `ref_publish` and `ref_drop` audit events currently carry no ref transaction ID, so writer-side append ordering had to be inferred through `blob_storage_log`.

topic: A sealed ref snapshot carries its own fold
canonical_claim: A sealed ref snapshot carries its own fold cursor, and the ref log may be trimmed only through that cursor.

topic: A Live or Removing namespace row requires a
canonical_claim: A `Live` or `Removing` namespace row requires a readable `_ckpt` carrying `life_epoch`; only `Creating` is exempt during the publish-before-flip window.

topic: Namespace creation publishes the _ckpt with life_epoch before
canonical_claim: Namespace creation publishes the `_ckpt` with `life_epoch` before flipping the catalog row to `Live`, while the janitor deletes `_ckpt` only when `catalog_cut.life_index.resolve(*life_id)` is false.

topic: republishRef performs a create-destination-shard CAS followed by a
canonical_claim: `republishRef` performs a create-destination-shard CAS followed by a drop-source-shard CAS, so a concurrent reader can observe both names or neither during the cross-shard window.

topic: Persisted ManifestRef fields use the wire keys me
canonical_claim: Persisted `ManifestRef` fields use the wire keys `me` for `writer_epoch`, `mb` for `build_sequence`, and `mo` for `manifest_ordinal`; no user-facing copy of these keys was found.

topic: resolveNamespaceLife performs one catalog read per retry-loop attempt
canonical_claim: `resolveNamespaceLife` performs one catalog read per retry-loop attempt, re-observes the result after each catalog mutation attempt, and is bounded by `kMaxResolveAttempts = 32`.

topic: Before refusing a closed removal admission, namespaceLife reconciles
canonical_claim: Before refusing a closed removal admission, `namespaceLife` reconciles a fresh catalog cut so an absent or replaced row can detach a dead predecessor and free the logical namespace name.

topic: Fixture helpers use CasRefCatalog::lifeIfCataloged(backend, layout, ns).value_or(fixture::
canonical_claim: Fixture helpers use `CasRefCatalog::lifeIfCataloged(backend, layout, ns).value_or(fixture::fixtureLife(ns))`, so an admitted catalog life wins and the deterministic fixture identity is used only when no catalog entry exists.

topic: When checkpoint advancement fails, publishCkpt increments CasRefCkptNotAdvanced, calls
canonical_claim: When checkpoint advancement fails, publishCkpt increments CasRefCkptNotAdvanced, calls advancePublishBackoff, and returns before the snapshot-adoption block; resetPublishBackoff and adoption occur together under one state_mutex hold after a successful CAS.

topic: planManifestCursorPage is called only when !suppress_destructive; at that
canonical_claim: `planManifestCursorPage` is called only when `!suppress_destructive`; at that point `frontier_complete` implies `universe_authoritative`, so its `catalog_recovery_authoritative` argument is true whenever the gate opens.

topic: planManifestCursorPage freezes LIST candidates and exact-GET bytes and
canonical_claim: `planManifestCursorPage` freezes LIST candidates and exact-GET bytes and tokens before `readAdoptedFoldSeal` and the `CasRefCatalog::read` cut; it performs no fresh GET after the cut, rejects identity mismatches with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and a token change prevents `deleteExact`.

topic: planManifestCursorPage freezes at most nomination_budget well-formed candidates before
canonical_claim: `planManifestCursorPage` freezes at most `nomination_budget` well-formed candidates before performing exact GETs; a well-formed key beyond the cap is retained with `budget_exhausted` instead of reaching the old `chassert`.

topic: If the namespace fan-out or recovery-operation budget is
canonical_claim: If the namespace fan-out or recovery-operation budget is exhausted, `activeManifestKeys` marks `NamespaceProtection::recovery_incomplete`, and the planner discards partial protection sets and retains every candidate in that namespace under `SweepRetainClass::WorkBudgetExhausted`.

topic: folded.mf_cleanup is one-shot rather than durable across GC
canonical_claim: `folded.mf_cleanup` is one-shot rather than durable across GC rounds: the same round advances the ref-log cursor past the owner-removal transaction before `manifest_deletes`, so budget-declined manifests are reclaimed by the orphan-manifest sweep instead of being reintroduced by the next fold.

topic: CatalogLifecycleReconciler::reconcile selects an eligible completed-removal row before app
canonical_claim: `CatalogLifecycleReconciler::reconcile` selects an eligible completed-removal row before applying the component-level clean-return fence; an eligible row always calls `CasRefCatalog::deleteCompletedRemovingAtSnapshot`, and a fence loss resolves that exact row as `ExactRowStillPresent`.

topic: The reconciler's eligible-row path performs the initial selection
canonical_claim: The reconciler's eligible-row path performs the initial selection `GET` and the primitive's mandatory resolution `GET`, without adding another catalog read; a genuinely clean no-eligible cut retains its component-level fence check before returning the final snapshot.

topic: CatalogLifecycleReconciler owns deterministic eligible-row selection and the N
canonical_claim: `CatalogLifecycleReconciler` owns deterministic eligible-row selection and the `N + 1` complete-catalog rescan loop for adopted-parent completed-removal draining.

topic: CatalogLifecycleReconciler returns authority, exact-row resolution, retired predecessor li
canonical_claim: `CatalogLifecycleReconciler` returns authority, exact-row resolution, retired predecessor lives, the final clean catalog cut, and the deletion count to its caller.
